overview.title: Agentic AI Course - 10 weeks, about 5 hours a week
rules: Week 0: set up and take the skills check. Pick a capstone project on the Project Options tab.
Each week has 5 Required days, one deliverable each, ending in a pass/fail gate. Stretch and Optional steps are extras.
Weeks 1-2 are done by hand, without an AI assistant. From Week 3 assistants are allowed.
Use only public or synthetic data. Never put real customer data, keys or secrets in the capstone repo.
Model API spend for Weeks 3-10 is roughly USD 10-25 per person. Use an API key with a spend limit.

routing.title: Skills check routing (Week 0 Day 2)
routing.fast: 5/5 easy CodingBat Python problems (Warmup-1, String-1, List-1) in 30 minutes without AI: fast-track. Week 1 Days 1-4 become Stretch; you still must pass the Week 1 gate.
routing.full: Fewer than 5/5: full track. Do every Week 1 and Week 2 Required day; use the Week 1 Stretch steps for extra practice.

links.label: CodingBat Python problems (skills check and Week 1 gate; no account needed to solve)
futurecoder.io: free in-browser Python course with hints (extra practice for the full track)

courses.name: Building with the Claude API (Anthropic Academy)
Context engineering: "Context management" lesson (Claude Academy, Claude Platform 101)
Introduction to Model Context Protocol (Anthropic Academy)
Model Context Protocol: Advanced Topics (Anthropic Academy)
Context engineering: "Effective context engineering for AI agents" (Anthropic guide, listed by Claude Academy)
Resilience: "Claude API errors" - retries with backoff, 429/529/504, request IDs (Anthropic docs)
Resilience: "Rate limits" - limits, retry-after, spend limits (Anthropic docs)
Observability: "Observability with OpenTelemetry" - traces, metrics, logs for agents (Claude Agent SDK docs)
Observability: "Track cost and usage" (Claude Agent SDK docs)
Observability: "Monitoring" reference - every metric and event (Claude Code docs)
Resilience in production: "Hosting the Agent SDK" (Claude Agent SDK docs)

courseNotes.text: Claude Academy (formerly Anthropic Academy) course catalog
Claude Academy has no dedicated courses on context engineering, observability or resilience (checked 2026-10-06), so those steps use Anthropic's official guides and docs.

worth.text: Kleppmann's Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd ed., 2026) is a paid book. Its chapters are Optional steps; the free Cambridge lecture series and notes are the Required path.
Model API spend: plan about USD 10-25 per person and use a sandbox API key with a spend limit.
Practice data: every option uses a public or synthetic dataset. The ticket dataset is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial learning use).
Python in 2 weeks is the riskiest part for limited coders; the skills check plus Stretch steps cover the gap.
Google's managed agent hosting is now documented as Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine).
The original DataRobot agent templates repo is deprecated; this plan uses its successor, the DataRobot Agent Application template.

planIntro: Required = the weekly core. Stretch = free extras for faster learners. Optional = paid book, platform account, or an alternative.

roadmap.title: Project roadmap: turning each week's learning into project progress
roadmap.intro: Each week, what you learn becomes one step of your capstone. The Project Options tab shows what each step looks like for your chosen option. By week 10 you have one working, measured, hardened agent - not 10 separate exercises.

0.learn: Tooling: Python, uv, VS Code, Git, GitHub
0.apply: Create the project repo. Pick an option. Write the 1-page spec (Project Planning tab, step 1).
0.state: A repo with a README, the spec and a link to the dataset
0.doneWhen: README names the option; spec has all 8 sections filled

1.learn: Python core: functions, loops, lists, dicts, files
1.apply: Write plain-Python helpers you will reuse: load a record, count labels, clean text.
1.state: A small library of tested helper functions in the repo
1.doneWhen: Helpers run on 20 real records from your dataset

2.learn: Applied Python: JSON/CSV, HTTP, errors, pytest, async, Docker, Git branches
2.apply: Build the ingest step: load your dataset into typed records, with tests, in Docker. Work on a branch and merge by pull request.
2.state: Phase 1 done: data flows in reliably
2.doneWhen: `docker run` ingests 100 records; 10 tests green; 1 PR merged

3.learn: LLM APIs, prompting, structured output, tool calling
3.apply: Add the first model step: classify or extract with JSON output, plus 2 tools. Record first metrics in the README.
3.state: The project makes its first useful decision
3.doneWhen: 50/50 valid JSON, accuracy >= 70%, cost and latency in README

4.learn: RAG: embeddings, vector store, chunking, recall@k
4.apply: Give the project knowledge: index your option's documents, retrieve with citations.
4.state: Answers are grounded in your own data
4.doneWhen: recall@5 >= 0.70 on 20 questions; answers cite chunk ids

5.learn: Agent design, MCP servers, Claude Code, spec-driven development (OpenSpec, Spec Kit)
5.apply: Wrap your capabilities as 3 MCP tools; let an agent loop choose them. Start using Claude Code with plan-then-code. From now on, every feature starts as a spec change that the coding agent builds from.
5.state: A real agent that uses your tools

6.apply: Rebuild the agent as a graph with memory. Write 30 eval cases and one command that scores them.
6.doneWhen: Eval runs in one command; baseline numbers recorded

7.apply: Try a multi-agent version against the same evals. Keep it only if the numbers justify it. Record the decision.

8.learn: Timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, idempotency, queues, rate limits, load tests
8.apply: Make the agent survive failures: retry safely, never act twice, queue work, load-test it.
8.state: The agent keeps working when things fail

9.learn: OpenTelemetry, dashboards, alarms, runbooks, cost; managed hosting
9.apply: Instrument every model and tool call; add a dashboard, an alarm and a runbook. Compare hosting platforms for your project.
9.state: You can see, and get alerted on, what the agent does
9.doneWhen: Trace shows every tool call; alarm fires in a test; runbook covers 3 alerts

10.learn: OWASP agentic risks, prompt-injection red team, least privilege, audit logs
10.apply: Threat-model the project, red-team it, cut tool permissions, add an audit log. Write the final report vs baseline.
10.state: Phase 6 done: a secured, measured agent with a write-up
10.doneWhen: <= 1 of 20+ injections succeeds; final report with metrics vs baseline

planning.title: Project planning: from specification to phases to code
intro: A simple, repeatable way to plan the capstone: write a short spec, split it into phases, then build each phase in small tested steps. Keep the spec and plan in your repo and update them as you learn.

Plan progressively. In weeks 0-2 you cannot plan the whole project, and you are not expected to. Start with a rough spec v0, plan only the next phase in detail, and add metrics, targets, risks and decisions as each week teaches you enough to decide them. The "Example - Data Analyst Agent" tab shows what to plan in each week (green column).

steps.title: Step 1 - Write a 1-page specification (Week 0, update weekly)

rows.text: Problem
Who has the problem and what it costs them today.
Support engineers spend time routing tickets; misroutes delay answers.
Users
Who uses the agent and how they interact with it.
A support engineer reviews the agent's suggestion in a queue.
Inputs and outputs
What goes in, what comes out, in what format.
In: ticket text. Out: JSON {queue, priority, answer or escalate, citations}.
Success metrics
The 5 numbers you will measure, with targets.
Accuracy >= 80%, cost/ticket <= $0.01, p95 <= 8 s, escalation 10-25%, 0 duplicate actions.
Non-goals
What you will deliberately NOT build.
No auto-reply to customers; no access to real customer data.
Data
Which public dataset, its license, how you split it.
HF customer-support-tickets (CC BY-NC), English only; 30 cases held out for evals.
Risks and unknowns
What could go wrong and how you will find out early.
Labels may be noisy - check 20 by hand in week 3.
Phases
The phase list from step 2, with dates.
Phases 1-6 below, one row per phase.

steps.title: Step 2 - Split the spec into phases (each phase ends at a weekly gate)

rows.text: 1. Foundations
Data flows in reliably, tested and containerized.
Week 2 gate passed.
Data model and folder layout.
2. Model core
The model makes a useful, grounded decision.
Week 3 and 4 gates passed.
Prompt and output schema; chunking choice.
3. Agent
An agent uses your tools, with a measured baseline.
Week 5 and 6 gates passed; baseline recorded.
Tool list and eval set design.
4. Architecture choice
Single vs multi-agent, decided by numbers.
Week 7 gate passed; decision record written.
The comparison method and the decision rule.
5. Production hardening
Survives failures and is observable.
Week 8 and 9 gates passed.
Failure modes list; alerts and runbook outline.
6. Secure and ship
Secured, audited, written up.
Week 10 gate passed; final report.
Threat model.

refs.label: Shape Up (free book on shaping work)

steps.title: Step 3 - Build each phase in small steps (the same loop every week)

rows.text: Break down
Turn the phase into 3-6 GitHub issues, each finishable in one sitting.
Every issue has a clear "done when".
Design note
For anything non-trivial, write 5-10 lines: approach, alternatives, why.
Note is in the issue or a docs/ file.
Test first
Write the test or eval case that proves the issue is done.
The test fails for the right reason.
Code
Make the test pass with the simplest code. From week 5, write the issue as a spec change first (OpenSpec or Spec Kit), then have Claude Code build from it: explore, plan, then code.
Tests pass locally and in Docker.
Review and merge
Open a pull request, read your own diff, get one peer review.
PR merged to main.
Measure and update
Run the evals, update the README metrics table, the spec and the decision log.
README numbers match the latest eval run.
Demo
Show the week's progress in the 30-minute group demo.
Gate result shown with numbers.

planning.tip: Tip: keep three living files in the repo - SPEC.md (step 1), PLAN.md (step 2 with issue links) and DECISIONS.md (one entry per design choice). Claude Code reads them as context, so they also make the AI assistant more useful.

example.title: Worked example: execution roadmap for the Data Analyst Agent (talk to my data)
intro: The agent answers business questions over the public Chinook music-store database (SQLite) by writing and running read-only SQL, then returns a short, chart-ready summary.

This tab shows what can realistically be built each week with what the course has taught so far. Nobody can plan the whole project in weeks 0-2, so the green column shows the planning you do each week: the spec and plan grow as your skills grow.
Use it as a model: copy this tab, then rewrite each row for your own option, keeping the same rhythm.

rows.build: Create the repo. Download Chinook (SQLite). Open it with the sqlite3 command line and look at the 11 tables.
rows.deliverable: Repo with README and chinook.db instructions
rows.doneWhen: README lists the 11 tables and 3 questions you would like to ask the data
rows.planning: Spec v0 - only what you know today: problem, users, data source and license, 3 example questions. Leave metrics and phases blank.

rows.learn: Python core: functions, loops, lists, dicts
rows.build: Use Python's sqlite3 module to run 5 hand-written SQL queries and print the results as lists of dicts.
rows.deliverable: queries.py with 5 working functions, one per question
rows.doneWhen: 5 functions run and their results match running the same SQL in the sqlite3 shell
rows.planning: Grow the question list to 10 plain-English questions. For each, note the tables and the hand-written SQL that answers it - these become your first gold answers.

rows.learn: JSON/CSV, errors, pytest, Docker, Git branches
rows.build: Package the query layer: a CLI that takes SQL, runs it read-only, returns JSON. Bad SQL and empty results return clear errors, not tracebacks. Tests and Docker.
rows.deliverable: Phase 1 done: a safe, tested, containerized query runner
rows.doneWhen: Write statements are refused (read-only mode); 10 tests green in Docker; work merged by pull request
rows.planning: Spec v1: fix the input/output format (question in, JSON answer out). Break Phase 2 into 3-5 GitHub issues. Only plan the next phase in detail.

rows.learn: LLM API, prompting, structured output, tool calling
rows.build: First AI step: send the question plus the table list to Claude and get back JSON {intent, tables, sql}. Run the SQL with your Week 2 runner.
rows.deliverable: Natural-language question to SQL, end to end
rows.doneWhen: 20/20 outputs are valid JSON; at least 12/20 queries return the gold result; cost and latency in the README
rows.planning: Add success metrics with your first real numbers (accuracy, cost per question, latency). Note what fails - these failures shape Week 4.

rows.build: Give the model knowledge: index the schema (one chunk per table with column descriptions) and 20 example question-SQL pairs; retrieve the relevant ones for each question.
rows.doneWhen: Retrieval puts the right tables in the top 5 for at least 16/20 questions; gold-result matches improve on Week 3
rows.planning: Add risks you have now seen: ambiguous questions, wrong joins, large results. Draft Phase 3 issues (tools and agent loop).

rows.learn: Agent design, MCP, Claude Code, spec-driven development
rows.build: Build an MCP server with 3 tools: list_tables, describe_table, run_sql (read-only). Let an agent loop decide which to call. Write the tool tests as a spec change (OpenSpec or Spec Kit) and have Claude Code build them.
rows.deliverable: A real agent that explores the schema before writing SQL
rows.doneWhen: MCP Inspector lists 3 tools; 8/10 scripted questions answered correctly through the tools
rows.planning: Write your first decision record: why an agent loop (or a fixed workflow) for this project. Plan Phase 3 week 6: the eval set.

rows.build: Rebuild as a graph: understand question, explore schema, write SQL, run, summarize. Add memory so follow-ups work ("and for 2012?"). Build 30 eval questions with gold result sets and one eval command.
rows.doneWhen: Eval runs 30 questions in one command; accuracy, cost, p50/p95 latency and clarification rate recorded
rows.planning: Now you know enough to set real targets: spec v2 with target numbers based on the baseline. Plan Phase 4.

rows.build: Try a handoff version: SQL writer, then SQL checker (validates against the schema and runs EXPLAIN), then summariser. Run the same 30 evals.
rows.doneWhen: Table of accuracy, cost, p50, p95 for single vs multi; keep multi only if +5 points at no more than 2x cost
rows.planning: Decision record: single or multi, with the numbers. Update the plan if the architecture changed.

rows.learn: Timeouts, retries, idempotency, queues, rate limits, load tests
rows.build: Add a query timeout, retries with backoff for model calls, a result cache keyed by normalized SQL, and a rate limit. Load-test with 50 simulated users.
rows.deliverable: An agent that stays up under load and failure
rows.doneWhen: 50-user load test: under 1% errors; slow queries stopped at the timeout; repeated questions served from cache
rows.planning: Add a failure-modes list to the spec (slow query, model overload, huge result). Plan Phase 5 week 9.

rows.build: Trace each question: model calls, tool calls, SQL run time, rows returned. Dashboard plus a slow-query alarm. Runbook for the top 3 alerts. Compare hosting options.
rows.deliverable: You can see and get alerted on what the agent does
rows.doneWhen: One trace shows every model and tool call; the slow-query alarm fires in a test; runbook covers 3 alerts
rows.planning: Decision record: where you would host it and why. Draft the final-report outline.

rows.learn: OWASP agentic risks, red team, least privilege, audit logs
rows.build: Red-team it: prompt injection in questions, attempts to make it write or drop data, SQL injection. Database user is read-only; every query goes to an audit log.
rows.deliverable: Phase 6 done: a secured, measured agent and a final report
rows.doneWhen: At least 20 attack attempts with at most 1 success; 0 write queries ever executed; audit-log count equals queries run
rows.planning: Final report: spec vs reality, metrics vs baseline, decisions, what you would do next.
